summary: the app-studio lock now follows cd, git -C and the remote of a push, so an app thread can no longer commit or push to app-studio through 'cd ../app-studio && git push', and a command for the app typed from an app-studio folder is no longer refused
appCreator: A thread in your app can no longer commit or push to app-studio by changing folder inside the command; before, that form slipped past the lock.

A commit or push for your own app is no longer refused just because the thread's shell happened to sit in an app-studio folder. When the lock does refuse, its message names the folder and remote it judged.

skipped.reason: checked by hand at the #350 checkpoints

notVerified: A folder only the shell can work out (cd $VAR, cd $(...)) is refused only when its text names app-studio; the lock stays a strong guard, not a lock (GOVERNANCE section 2).
Windows shells (cmd, PowerShell syntax) are not parsed; only POSIX shell command lines.
